title: Combat and gameplay animation
summary: Animation that communicates gameplay intent and outcome while staying synchronized with input, movement, hit detection, camera, sound, effects, and replicated state.

designKnowledge.rigAndDeformation: Choose a rig that supports the intended poses and gameplay-visible deformation. Test extreme poses and transitions, not only a neutral idle.
designKnowledge.integration: A gameplay event contract coordinates presentation; client animation does not decide server damage.

technicalPatterns.name: Treat gameplay windows as explicit state
technicalPatterns.guidance: Tie hit windows, movement restrictions, interruption, and recovery to a documented state/event contract; verify implemented animation timing in Studio.

technicalPatterns.name: Design transitions and cancellation
technicalPatterns.guidance: Specify transitions from attack to hit reaction, dodge, stun, death, and locomotion. Test interrupted and repeated inputs.

technicalPatterns.name: Keep artistic approval human
technicalPatterns.guidance: Automated timing and consistency checks may triage issues. Hero animation and final art direction require independent human visual sign-off.

dependencies.rationale: Use documented Roblox animation authoring capabilities for the selected rig and workflow.
Gameplay outcomes remain server-owned even when animation feedback is presented locally.

failureModes.description: Damage timing drifts from the visible pose or effects.
failureModes.mitigation: Use a shared event contract and test active windows under interruption and multiplayer replication.

failureModes.description: A missing transition leaves the character visually or mechanically locked.
failureModes.mitigation: Test all exits, cancellation, respawn, and track cleanup for each combat state.

scenarios.action: Exercise attack, hit, block, dodge, stagger, death, and return-to-locomotion transitions.
scenarios.expected: Poses remain readable and gameplay input recovers at the specified boundary.

scenarios.action: Compare attacker and observer views in a two-client Studio session.
scenarios.expected: The confirmed combat result and visible sequence agree with the declared timing model.

acceptanceCriteria: The animation has a documented state and event contract.
Weight, timing, contact, silhouette, transition, and responsiveness are reviewed.
Hero animation receives explicit human approval.

considerations: Measure active tracks and effects under representative combat concurrency on the midrange mobile baseline.
Avoid excessive simultaneous tracks and effects that obscure other players or exhaust frame-time budgets.

evidence.description: Animation quality dimensions, integrated timing, transition failures, and repeatable review scenarios are specified.

assumptions: Specific rigs, animation graphs, and APIs must be verified against current Studio workflow before implementation.
AI analysis is assistive and cannot certify artistic excellence.
